objective: Use a full-scale manual separating screen to recover dry ceramic finishing media from an intermixed batch into a collection receiver while retaining every representative steel washer in the screen, then leave the released screen stably resting on its supports. This frozen contract specifies prospective rigid-PhysX construction and validation; it does not claim that component physics or a robot demonstration already passes.
instruction: Use the separating screen to recover the finishing media into the collection tray, keeping all metal parts in the screen. Leave the screen resting on its supports.
industrial_mapping: Category: Impact on jobs. The mapped occupation is Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers (SOC 51-9061.00; approximately 0.6 million US workers under the review prompt). O*NET record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb defines this occupation as sorting processed or machined parts and lists the regular task “Grade, classify, or sort products according to sizes, weights, colors, or other specifications,” plus handling and moving materials. Raytech primary records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc establish manual screening as an actual dry mass-finishing parts/media separation operation rather than an invented industrial label. The tested ability is physical size-and-orientation separation, bridge release, bimanual loaded-tool control, spill prevention, workpiece retention, and stable release—not visual classification alone. Closed, unmerged PR684 is disclosed as historical overlap in apertured sifting. Current catalog and six-suite checks found no active, accepted, pending, own-team, or benchmark task with this same industrial endpoint, although novelty must be checked again immediately before submission.
damage_rules: At reset freeze M as the 24 single-body media assemblies; WA as four washer assemblies; WS(a) as the four rigid arc-segment bodies belonging to washer assembly a; WS=union of WS(a); S, R, U, C, G, and T as screen, receiver, supports, feed cup, robot/gripper, and table/floor collider-body sets. A washer assembly reference position x_a(k) is its mass-weighted segment center of mass, x_a=Σ_{s∈WS(a)}m_s x_s/Σm_s. Its frozen assembly mass m_a is Σ_{s∈WS(a)}m_s and is counted exactly once in admission and F. Washer orientation is the mass-weighted principal frame reconstructed from all segment transforms; no individual segment is a batch assembly.

Each washer has four authored breakable fixed joints with an assumed 200 N force threshold. At physics sample k, washer joint force is |J_constraint|/dt for each joint constraint impulse after the solve. Fracture latches if a joint is reported broken, its connected-segment relative transform differs from its authored transform by more than 0.0005 m or 0.5 degrees, or |J_constraint|/dt reaches 200 N. The four values are maximized over joints and 240 Hz samples for washer_fixed_joint_force_sample_max.

For every completed physics step k: resolve PhysX; sample transforms, velocities, joint states, signed distances, contact and constraint impulses; convert each impulse J over dt=1/240 s to average force |J|/dt; advance transfer state machines; latch immutable events; update containment and recovery; update dwell; then compute score. O_0 is the settled reset observation and O_57600 is processed before timeout. Cameras are sampled independently at 20 Hz.

The reset-stability measurement begins only after a two-second, robot-stationary settling period and uses the following untouched three-second window of 720 physics intervals. Screen translation drift is max_k ||x_S(k)-x_S(k_start)|| over that window. Rotation drift is max_k geodesic_angle(q_S(k),q_S(k_start)). Batch speed is max over every sample and every body in M∪WS of ||v_b(k)||. All three accumulators reset between validation trials.

Define p(a,b,k)=max(0,-d_signed(a,b,k)), where d_signed is the minimum post-solve collider separation in metres and negative values denote overlap. Screen-fixture penetration is max over every 240 Hz sample and collider pair S×(R∪U∪T). Dynamic penetration is max over every sample and pair having at least one collider body in M∪WS and the other in M∪WS∪S∪R∪C∪T. Touching at d_signed=0 has zero penetration.

For screen_external_contact_force_sample_max, at each 240 Hz sample sum the magnitudes of all post-solve contact impulses over all manifolds and contact points whose pair has exactly one collider in S and the other in G∪R∪U∪C∪T∪M∪WS; count each unordered collider pair once and exclude internal S-S contacts. Divide that scalar impulse sum by dt, then take the maximum over samples. This is deliberately a conservative screen-wide load, not a per-contact peak.

Each assembly b∈M∪WA follows FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN. For media, its reference is its rigid-body center of mass. For a washer, its reference is x_a and every transition additionally requires all four segments to be on the same permitted side of the crossed boundary at the destination sample. A swept crossing uses the straight segment between consecutive reference samples. FEED means the reference and all washer segments, when applicable, are inside the feed-cup interior. EXITED_FEED requires outward mouth crossing. FREE_FLIGHT requires a later sample outside cup and screen. ENTERED_SCREEN requires a later inward rim crossing and all washer segments inside_screen.

Mixture-body contacts and transient cup-rim contacts are permitted during admission. Individual robot contact with M or WS, staging-surface contact, receiver entry, non-mouth cup departure, a washer segment crossing a boundary inconsistently with its assembly reference, or any segment separating from its assembly invalidates provenance. batch_loaded latches only when every media and washer assembly has validly reached ENTERED_SCREEN and all washer segments are currently inside_screen.

Washer loss latches if any washer segment exits over the screen rim after admission, crosses below the perforated plane without its assembly reference and all segments following a genuine clear-aperture path, contacts T outside R, becomes inaccessible, or has invalid provenance. Segment re-entry cannot clear the event.

Media spill latches if any medium exits over the screen rim after admission, contacts T outside R, enters R without a prior genuine aperture crossing, exits R after entry, crosses the screen floor outside a clear aperture, becomes inaccessible, or has invalid provenance. It is immutable even if the body is recovered; the body remains physically present and movable.

Receiver contamination latches if any segment in WS or any body in C∪S∪U, or any other non-media task body, has its center inside_receiver. Washer fracture, receiver contamination, invalid provenance, washer loss, and media spill are immutable score-zero events.

A body is inaccessible when its center is outside the frozen reachable-workspace polytope, below z_table-0.02 m, or inside an authored closed fixture volume for which every predefined gripper approach corridor intersects collision geometry. A washer assembly is inaccessible if any segment is inaccessible. This predicate is deterministic and independent of IK failure.

Any post-reset pose or velocity write to M∪WS∪S∪R∪U∪C, fake grasp weld, required-collider disable, particle freeze, or hidden restoring force is also an immutable hard failure. Breakage, spill, loss, contamination, force exceedance, and over-rim escape must remain physically possible; no velocity ceiling, collision suppression, state correction, or hidden return force may prevent them. Physics-validation thresholds do not alter task score unless the resulting state independently satisfies a scoring or hard-failure predicate.
assets: Independently authored full-scale separating screen: sourced 0.3683 m outer diameter and 0.0635 m depth; assumed 0.0127 m clear square apertures, 0.003 m ribs and floor, 0.0157 m pitch, 0.150 m perforated-floor radius, 0.003 m walls, 0.40 kg mass, and two 0.040×0.018×0.005 m grasp tabs.

Twenty-four free rigid ceramic angle-cut cylinders: sourced 0.009525 m diameter by 0.022225 m axial envelope; assumed parallel 15-degree cuts and 2500 kg/m^3 density. Record each realized closed-mesh mass and inertia; analytic reference mass is 0.0035044969 kg.

Four independently authored representative plain carbon-steel washer assemblies: 0.030 m outer diameter, 0.008 m bore, 0.004 m thickness, 7850 kg/m^3 density, and four rigid arc segments joined by breakable fixed joints. Analytic summed segment mass is 0.0206170159 kg per washer; no commercial SKU is claimed.

Rigid receiver 0.45×0.40×0.08 m with 0.005 m floor and walls; two 0.52×0.015×0.010 m support beams with four legs; rigid feed cup 0.078 m outer diameter by 0.100 m high with 0.003 m walls and floor and 0.10 kg empty mass.
Pinned public YAM robot asset and guarded 14D left-seven/right-seven joint-action interface from the hash-indexed runtime snapshots.
Raytech primary records s-b442a7fa63fcb80c, s-a3efcebbecba0048, and s-855e796b5a3f8ecc; O*NET occupational record s-474cfcd0ccaa5ecb.
approximations: Only dry rigid-body separation is modeled. Polishing, abrasion, liquids, wet cohesion, dust, wear, lubrication, and material-property changes are excluded.

The 0.0127 m apertures, ribs, pitch, wall profile, screen mass, grasp tabs, 15-degree media cuts, ceramic density, fixtures, representative washer geometry, four-segment damage proxy, and 200 N joint threshold are explicit testable assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD, calibration results, or commercial-part specifications.

Initial uncalibrated contacts are ceramic/polymer static/dynamic friction 0.50/0.35, steel/polymer 0.45/0.35, media/media 0.40/0.30, restitution 0.05, contact offset 0.00015 m, rest offset 0 m, and 32/8 solver position/velocity iterations. Penetration, force, drift, joint-margin, and clearance thresholds are validation assumptions.

The batch starts entirely in the feed cup; screen and receiver start empty. Assumed centers are screen (0,0.25) m and cup (0.31,0.25) m. Support-beam center y values are 0.15 and 0.35 m; support tops and the screen’s lowest reset geometry are z=0.13 m above the tabletop.

Measure clear-aperture width from collision geometry by intersecting the perforated floor with its plane, enumerating connected clear-space components inside the wall, and taking each component’s maximum inscribed axis-parallel segment.

End-first trials reset one medium 0.010 m above the center aperture with its long axis within 5 degrees of floor normal and zero velocity. Passage means its center crosses at least 0.005 m below the floor through that aperture within two seconds, with no rib-contact segment longer than 0.25 s. Use 20 deterministic azimuths and reset all state and accumulators per trial.

Transverse trials use the same reset with the long axis within 5 degrees of the floor plane. Bridge-release trials first require no passage for one second, then apply plus/minus 4-degree screen roll at 1 Hz for three seconds; release requires a genuine clear-aperture crossing. These prescribed motions belong only to component validation, not grading.

Washer escape trials place one intact washer assembly 0.005 m above the center aperture at 40 deterministic orientations spanning face-on, edge-on, and intermediate attitudes. Escape means its assembly reference crosses 0.005 m below the floor or any segment clears the floor without a permitted path. Bore-lodging trials place a medium nose against a washer bore at 20 relative azimuths, apply gravity for two seconds, lift the washer 0.02 m, and classify lodging when the medium remains mechanically carried for one second without robot contact.

Bilateral grip requires resolved positive-normal-force contacts between both opposing collider sides of each gripper pinch and its screen grasp tab. Any false 240 Hz sample resets duration. Loaded lift is the minimum world-z point of S minus its settled-reset value. A stationary hold sample additionally requires all M and all WS inside_screen, lift of at least 0.030 m, maximum S body speed of 0.010 m/s, and no hard failure.

Joint margins are measured for every controlled non-fixed robot joint at every 240 Hz sample from the first guarded action through final release clearance. Lower margin is q-q_lower and upper margin is q_upper-q; aggregate each as the minimum over joints and samples.

Camera checks use rendered 20 Hz control frames. Valid RGB pixels are finite and in encoded range; valid depth pixels are finite and positive. Required visibility means at least one unoccluded projected pixel exists for the screen, cup, receiver, one medium, and one complete washer assembly, without identifier overlays. Per-frame validity takes the minimum across required cameras; visibility fraction is qualifying frames divided by all control frames.

Refinement replays identical seeds, resets, transforms, action timestamps, and held 20 Hz actions at 240 and 480 Hz for seeds 0 through 4. Recovery delta is the maximum seed-paired absolute final-r difference. Event-count delta is the maximum paired absolute difference in the number of distinct immutable event types latched. Every trial resets state machines, dwell, events, and metric accumulators.

Pinned scene.py explicitly sets physics dt=1/240 s and supports control_hz=20, giving 12 physics intervals per control action. simulation_cfg.py exposes configurable dt for prospective 480 Hz refinement. Source inspection establishes configuration only, not passed task physics.

Scripted experts may read poses, velocities, joints, contacts, and scorer flags while leaving model observations unchanged. They may not write task-object states, teleport objects, create fake welds, remove required collisions, freeze particles, or apply hidden restoring forces.

Construction readiness means the mechanism is specified sufficiently to attempt native component tests. Native passage, bridging, retention, YAM grasping, demonstrations, refinement agreement, portability, and submission readiness remain unverified.
scoring_spec: Freeze media assemblies M, washer assemblies WA, washer segments WS(a), and their reset masses. For each washer a, m_a=Σ_{s∈WS(a)}m_s and x_a(k)=Σm_s x_s(k)/m_a. Let M0=Σ_{i∈M}m_i+Σ_{a∈WA}m_a and MM0=Σ_{i∈M}m_i. inside_feed(b,k) means the assembly reference lies inside the cup inner-wall half-spaces and above its floor; for a washer it additionally requires every segment center inside those bounds. inside_screen(i,k) for media means its center is radially inside the screen wall, below its rim, and above the perforated plane except during genuine traversal. inside_screen(a,k) for a washer requires x_a and every segment center to satisfy those bounds and every fixed joint to remain intact. inside_receiver uses center position below the receiver rim, above its floor, and inside all inner-wall half-spaces; receiver contamination evaluates every washer segment separately. State transitions are sampled at 240 Hz after solve. valid_admission(b)=1 only after the complete causal FEED→EXITED_FEED→FREE_FLIGHT→ENTERED_SCREEN chain without a provenance fault; washer transitions use x_a and the all-segment constraints. admitted_mass(k)=Σ_{i∈M}m_i valid_admission(i)+Σ_{a∈WA}m_a valid_admission(a). F(k)=clamp(admitted_mass/M0,0,1), with each washer mass counted once. batch_loaded latches only when every assembly has valid admission and all washer segments are inside_screen. A genuine aperture crossing is a downward swept media-center segment through the floor plane that intersects exactly one connected clear-space aperture and no rib collider. eligible_receiver(i,k)=1 only when batch_loaded has latched, medium i has valid admission and a later genuine aperture crossing, is currently inside_receiver, and has never spilled, become inaccessible, intersected a receiver wall, or incurred invalid provenance. r(k)=clamp(Σ_{i∈M}m_i eligible_receiver(i,k)/MM0,0,1). Exiting the receiver latches spill before scoring, so eligibility cannot be recovered. washer_retained(k) requires every joint intact, every washer assembly validly admitted, and every segment currently inside_screen. supported(k) requires resolved S-U contact on both support beams, lowest screen geometry within 0.002 m of support tops, |roll|≤3 degrees, |pitch|≤3 degrees, and the screen-center projection inside the support footprint. clear(k) requires minimum signed distance from every G collider to S∪M∪WS of at least 0.060 m. clean(k) means no immutable hard failure. Q(k)=1 iff batch_loaded, F=1, r≥0.98, washer_retained, supported, clear, and clean. Start dwell at k0 when Q first becomes true; that sample contributes zero elapsed time. D(k)=1 only after Q remains true for k-k0≥720 consecutive physics intervals. Any false Q resets k0 and immediately revokes D. Before hard-failure override, B(k)=0.20F+0.70 clamp(r/0.98,0,1)+0.10D. Final score is permanently zero after any hard failure and otherwise equals B. Report at 20 Hz from the latest completed physics sample and process O_57600 before timeout. Untouched score is 0; complete valid loading with no recovery is 0.20; F=1 with exactly 12 of 24 equal-mass media eligible gives 0.5571428571; F=1 and r≥0.98 without dwell gives 0.90; valid three-second released dwell gives 1.00. Hand identity, action count, shake count, and prescribed action order are not graded.
